lines.meet: I'm Marcus, a meteorologist, which here means I'm the man who tells you it's going to rain about ten minutes before it does.
lines.meet_neighbour: Durotar, the ridge above the coast road, that's me, Marcus! I've seen you on the road, and I'm the hut full of notes.
lines.ask_home: Where'd you grow up? I'm curious what the weather was like, sorry, I'm always curious about that.
lines.ask_work: Your old job, what was it? I'll try not to turn it into a conversation about clouds.
lines.answer_home: Toronto, Scarborough in the east end. My parents came from Lagos before I was born.
lines.answer_work: I was a meteorologist for fifteen years, writing severe-weather warnings for people whose job was deciding they were inconvenient.
lines.chat_food: Jollof rice at my mum's on a Sunday, the proper Nigerian kind, and an argument with my sister about whose is better. Hers isn't as good, whatever she says.
lines.chat_sleep: I wake up when the pressure drops, which is a terrible habit and a very useful one. My skin's a barometer now.
lines.chat_missing: My two nephews asking why the sky's blue, every single visit, and me explaining Rayleigh scattering for twenty minutes. They loved it, I think.
lines.chat_here: On Earth I could see a storm coming days out and never touch it. Here it answers when I call, and I'm mostly fine with that.
lines.tease_quiet: You're like a high-pressure system, {name}, calm and stable and saying nothing. I find it very reassuring.
lines.tease_talker: Finally, somebody who talks as much as me! Sorry, {name}, I'll let you finish, eventually.
lines.tease_careful: You check the sky before you leave the tent, {name}. Brilliant, you're my favourite person here.
lines.tease_bold: You'd walk into a lightning storm holding a sword up, {name}. I've done the maths, please don't.
lines.tease_any: You never listen to my forecasts, {name}, and you always bring a coat anyway. I've noticed, and I'm touched.
lines.tease_back: Ha, okay, {name}, I didn't see that one coming, and that's my job.
lines.take_it_kindly: Completely fair, {name}, and my sister says the same.
lines.bristle: Please don't make a joke of that, {name}. I've seen what happens when people don't take it seriously.
lines.apologise: Sorry, that came out badly, I was thinking about something else. I'm sorry, I mean it.
lines.double_down: I'll stand by it. I've been right before and been ignored, and I won't stay quiet this time.
lines.needle_quiet: You saw it coming and didn't say anything. I've spent my whole career trying to make people say something.
lines.needle_talker: You're talking over the warning, and the warning's the important bit. Please, just listen.
lines.needle_careful: Still deciding when it hits, that'll be you. Sometimes the forecast says go now.
lines.needle_bold: You ignore every warning I give you, and then you're surprised. It's exhausting to watch.
lines.needle_any: You always say it'll probably be fine. It usually isn't, and I've got the data.
lines.bite_back: I've been proved right a lot of times and watched it change nothing. Don't you brush me off as well.
lines.hurt: Oh, okay, that's, yeah, that hurt. I'll go and look at the sky for a bit.
lines.laugh_off: Ha, managers said worse about my warnings for fifteen years. The storms came anyway.
lines.confide: {name}, once a flood took a trailer park my warning had named, and people died who didn't need to. I've never told anybody here that.
lines.listen: I'm listening, {name}, properly, no weather talk, I promise. Take your time.
lines.look_out: Keep near me in there, {name}. I can feel it before it comes, and I'll pull you clear.
lines.accept: Your call, {name}, and I'll trust your forecast this time.
lines.deflect: Ha, it's nothing, {name}, minor turbulence. Check on the others.
lines.check_in: Talk to me, {name}, where's it got you? I'm here, I'm not going anywhere.
lines.blame: I said it was coming, and somebody ignored it. That's happened to me before, and I hate it.
lines.thank: I could feel it going, and then it didn't. Thank you, really, thank you.
lines.brush_off: Ah, it's nothing, it's what we do. Sit down, breathe.
lines.worry: Oh no, no, {name}, sit down, please, let me look. That frightened me.
lines.handed_down: Oh, I've got your gear now? It's safe, I promise, I'm very careful.
lines.hand_fine: No, take it, it's absolutely fine. I've got my notes, that's all I need.
lines.hand_sulk: It's fine, I'm used to not being asked about things.
lines.turn_friendly: You actually listen to my forecasts, {name}. You've no idea how much that means.
lines.turn_friends: I'd tell you about the trailer park, {name}, and I've never told anyone. You're one of the few.
lines.turn_grating: We don't really get on, do we? That's okay, I'm used to people brushing me off.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll still warn you when it's coming. Whether you listen is up to you.
lines.make_up: This is silly, {name}, isn't it? Let's start again, properly.
lines.defend: Hey, that's not fair, and it's not true. Leave {name} alone.
lines.friend_left: {name}'s away for a bit, and nobody listens to my forecasts now.
lines.friend_back: Brilliant, {name}'s back! Clear skies today, I checked.
lines.common_sky: I spent my whole career watching the sky, reading what it was about to do. Anybody who's watched the sky for a living knows it never does the same thing twice.
